plan.topic: Clothes looser on tirzepatide but the scale barely moved: what SURMOUNT-1's waist-circumference result shows, and why the scale is only one measure
plan.angle: Reframe it as 'the scale is one measure among many': 'Jeans looser on tirzepatide? The scale isn't the only measure.' By 6 s: 'SURMOUNT-1 didn't only track weight. It also measured waist size.' Then give the 72-week average waist change, top dose vs placebo, in adults with obesity, or overweight plus at least one weight-related condition, without diabetes, copied exactly from NEJM 2022. Say it was measured alongside weight loss, and don't present it as a stand-in for weight loss. Drop 'the scale barely moved' from sentence 1 and the title. Suggested title: 'Tirzepatide: Why the Scale Is Only One Measure #shorts'. The DXA line is optional and keeps its full scope. Untagged tip: look at trends over time, and bring several measures, such as how clothes fit, waist, energy and labs, to your prescriber when you discuss progress. No dose or 'not working' talk, and no claim about any individual's fat loss.

plan.target_keyword: mounjaro losing inches but not weight
plan.why: Spin-off of L1. It turns L1's trial data into a felt body moment that sends viewers to the Weight Loss video. Its angle (non-scale measures) is new: no Short in the last 30 days has used it. | fact-check: The waist result is real and quotable: SURMOUNT-1 reported waist-circumference change by dose vs placebo at 72 weeks. The problem is the hook. 'Looser clothes, but the scale barely moved' sets up SURMOUNT-1 as an explanation for a weight stall. In the trial, waist and weight fell together, and no one studied people whose weight stalled while their waist shrank. Using the result to explain that experience implies body recomposition the data don't show. It also edges toward an individual claim ('your clothes prove you're losing fat'), which the angle itself bans. The DXA line (about three-quarters fat, 160-person substudy, doses pooled) also describes people who lost weight, not people whose weight held steady. A Short about a stalled scale also invites dose or 'not working' worries, so it needs the talk-to-your-prescriber route.

package.title: Tirzepatide: Jeans Looser? The Scale Isn't the Only Measure #shorts
package.description:
On tirzepatide and your jeans feel looser? SURMOUNT-1 tracked waist size alongside weight. In adults with obesity, or overweight plus at least one weight-related condition, without diabetes, average waist fell 18.5 cm over 72 weeks on the highest tirzepatide dose vs 4 cm on placebo, alongside weight loss, not instead of it. The scale is one measure, not the only one.
#Tirzepatide
Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

factcheck.summary: The Short is accurate and safe to ship. I checked the waist figures on the ACC SURMOUNT-1 trial summary: 15 mg −18.5 cm vs placebo −4.0 cm at week 72. The other doses were 5 mg −14.0 cm and 10 mg −17.7 cm. The same page confirms the trial population, including that people with diabetes were excluded. The PubMed record (PMID 35658024, Jastreboff et al., NEJM 2022;387:205-216) only showed a cookie page when I fetched it, so I couldn't read its text directly. The citation matches the published paper, and the script relies on it only for the population and for weight falling on average in both groups. Every number names the trial, the dose, the placebo comparison, the population and the 72-week timeframe. Waist is framed as a measure alongside weight loss, not instead of it. Our own tip and framing lines carry no source tag, the fixed safety line is one whole card, and there's no subscribe or "link in the description" line. I count 146 spoken words, which is inside the standard arm (135–160); the CTA note says about 148. The hook is a question and doesn't overpromise. Below are four minor wording and source-metadata fixes.

issues.problem: The house rule says never to shorten the obesity-trial population to "no diabetes". The stat label also drops "weight-related", so the muted card is narrower than what's spoken in s3.
issues.fix: on_screen_text: "SURMOUNT-1 (adults with obesity, or overweight + a weight-related condition, without diabetes): average waist change at 72 weeks, tirzepatide 15 mg −18.5 cm vs placebo −4.0 cm". stat_label: "SURMOUNT-1, tirzepatide 15 mg vs placebo (−4.0 cm), 72 weeks, adults with obesity or overweight + a weight-related condition, without diabetes"

issues.claim: Long stat sentence used as the caption source
issues.problem: Captions are built from this field. At this length it will run past 2 lines per card unless it's split into whole clauses, and a card must never end on a bare number.
issues.fix: Split the captions at whole clauses, for example: "SURMOUNT-1, 72 weeks: average waist change." / "Tirzepatide 15 mg: −18.5 cm." / "Placebo: −4.0 cm." Keep the full population on the stat card itself.

issues.problem: The ACC page shows a later update date, and the rules say to give the live revised date.
21 Jul 2022 is the print issue date. The paper was published online first on 4 Jun 2022.
